summary.text: Vivek Ramaswamy, a Republican entrepreneur who founded the biotechnology company Roivant Sciences in 2014, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Governor of Ohio to Amy Acton.
Born in Cincinnati, he ran for the 2024 Republican presidential nomination before endorsing Donald Trump.

paragraphs.text: Ramaswamy was born in Cincinnati, Ohio.
He graduated from Harvard College in 2007 with a degree in biology and received a J.D. from Yale Law School in 2013.
In 2014 he founded the biotechnology holding company Roivant Sciences, and he served as its chief executive until January 2021.
In 2022 he co-founded the investment firm Strive Asset Management.
Ramaswamy entered the 2024 Republican presidential primary, then withdrew and endorsed Donald Trump.
He launched his campaign for Ohio governor in February 2025, on a joint ticket with Robert McColley.
His running mate was state Senate President Rob McColley.
His platform called for eliminating the state income tax, lowering property taxes, universal school choice and reattaching work requirements to Medicaid and welfare.
He received 44.4% of the vote to Amy Acton's 52.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
